details: The pointwise claim $\mathrm Q_{\mathrm{req}}(\mathcal H;\mu)\ge\mathrm{VC}(\mathcal H)$ is false, even for uniform full-support $\mu$ on a finite domain. Angluin--Dohrn Theorem 25 instead gives an $\Omega(d)$ lower bound with a distribution chosen in its proof; it does not establish this coefficient-one bound for every fixed distribution.
name: Random Equivalence Queries Complexity / VC Dimension
proof_source: Survey Remark rem:random-query-vc-counterexample gives the explicit uniform-distribution witness. Original rejected record: sync/random_query_corrections/originals/025_random_equivalence_queries_complexity_vc_dimension.json.
witness_verification: Use the coded-singletons class with $n=3$, two code coordinates and three primary coordinates: $(00,000),(01,100),(10,010),(11,001)$. Its VC dimension is two: the two code coordinates are shattered and a class of four concepts cannot shatter three coordinates. Under uniform mass on the five coordinates, first propose the zero concept. Acceptance identifies it; a primary-coordinate counterexample identifies its singleton target, and a code-coordinate counterexample leaves at most two candidates, identifiable with one further proper query. The worst-case expected cost is at most $1+2/3=5/3<2$. Thus even proper random-query cost is below VC, and arbitrary cost is no larger. This is a strict finite gap, not an exact optimum or an unbounded-ratio witness.
